lessons.lesson: Every PARTICIPANT-facing write path must be backed by an explicit RLS policy or a SECURITY DEFINER RPC at design time — not discovered in post-spec security audit. The three HIGH findings (SA-002/003/007) were all writable paths that lacked one of these guards.

Postgres UPDATE policies cannot reference OLD in their WITH CHECK clause — only in USING. To prevent self-mutation of a field (e.g. role escalation), use a BEFORE UPDATE trigger with WHEN (NEW.field IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.field) rather than a WITH CHECK constraint.

Audit/log tables need their own INSERT policy. They are easy to skip because they are infrastructure, not user-facing. Without an INSERT policy, audit writes fail silently and the feature appears to work while producing no audit trail.

Offline-tolerant queues must use persistent storage (MMKV, AsyncStorage, SQLite) — never in-memory (globalThis, module-level arrays). In-memory queues are lost on app crash or background eviction. Design the storage layer first, not as an afterthought.

Validator WARN annotations are pre-mortems, not noise. Both WARN-2 (JuzTileAssignment missing last_updated_at → days_stalled hardcoded to 0) and the globalThis note became UAT conditions. Treat acknowledged warnings as deferred tasks that must be resolved, not silenced.

Large orchestration screens (500+ lines, 5+ concerns) should be split into ≥2 tasks. GroupKhatmScreen at 571 lines with 4 accordions, 3 bottom sheet refs, admin logic, realtime wiring, and stall computation was the largest single-task time sink (~14 min) and produced the days_stalled stub bug.

Multi-step client mutations that must be atomic (e.g. create group + copy participants) should be designed as SECURITY DEFINER RPCs from the start, not refactored in after a security audit. The start_new_cycle case required a post-spec migration because the original design used 4 sequential client calls.
Dark mode as a deferred Wave 5 audit sweep is an efficient pattern — avoids merge conflicts during component development and produces a single focused pass. Keep it as the last wave before E2E tests.

Deriving TypeScript types from the Postgres schema column-by-column before any implementation prevents downstream mismatches. The types.ts first-wave approach worked with zero type-level rework across 25 tasks.

Always exclude Supabase Deno edge function files from tsconfig.json. A root tsconfig with `"include": ["**/*.ts"]` will pull in supabase/functions/**/*.ts, causing `Cannot find name 'Deno'` errors across every edge function file. Add `"supabase/functions/**"` to the `exclude` array at design time, not after the typecheck gate fails.

Every Supabase edge function reachable via HTTP must verify a service-role Bearer token at the Deno.serve entry point — especially scheduler or dispatch functions that trigger side effects (push/email). The email-notifications function had this guard from the start; the notification-scheduler did not. Use email-notifications as the canonical auth pattern for all future edge functions.

Never include `detail: String(e)` or similar error serialization in HTTP response bodies from edge functions or API routes. Log the full error via console.error for server-side observability, but return only `{ "error": "Internal server error" }` to callers. Serializing caught exceptions leaks file paths, stack traces, and internal state.

After the threat model injects [threat-model] criteria into requirements.md, scan existing ACs for conflicts with the new security requirements. In this spec, US-1 AC-2 stated 'An account with this email already exists' which directly contradicted the injected enumeration-prevention criterion. The conflict should be resolved at injection time, not discovered by the validator.

Any task that installs a new package must list `package.json` (and `yarn.lock` or `package-lock.json`) in its Files array. In this spec T-4 listed only `src/lib/supabase.ts` but also added `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` to package.json. Missing this causes parallel agents to produce lockfile merge conflicts and misleads the file-conflict graph used to build parallel groups.

Deno edge function TypeScript under strict mode requires explicit type annotations on `.map()` callbacks when the source is an untyped Supabase query result. Use `: Record<string, unknown>` or a proper interface annotation — never rely on inference from `.select()` return types which Supabase types as `any` at runtime without codegen.

Zustand store tasks (wired: yes) have many implicit import sites rather than a single explicit callsite, making wired status harder to auto-verify during loop execution. When a store task is marked wired:yes, the verification should grep for the store export name across the full src/ tree, not just check for a specific consumer file.
